reference_memory.normal_pattern: The channel exhibits a dominant periodicity of ~20 points per cycle, consistent with the estimated period. Normal behavior includes three morphological modes: (1) low-amplitude triangular/sawtooth oscillations with gentle slopes and flat plateaus (e.g., candidate 0), (2) near-constant baselines with negligible variation (candidate 1), and (3) sharp, symmetric V- or U-shaped negative spikes recurring regularly every ~20 points, often followed by brief flat segments at trough level (candidate 2). Amplitude varies across segments: typical peak-to-trough ranges are 1.0–2.0 robust units in oscillatory segments, while spike segments reach ~0.7 units deep. Noise is minimal—most segments show near-zero MAD, indicating high stability. Trends are generally absent within individual windows, though long windows (e.g., candidate 3) may contain slow drifts or isolated transients; however, candidate 3’s large transient (peak >13) is inconsistent with other candidates and likely anomalous. Baseline levels shift between segments (e.g., median 0.0, +0.67, −0.67), reflecting non-stationary offset but not shape change. Acceptable variation includes minor slope differences, plateau duration shifts, and ±0.1–0.2 amplitude jitter—but not sustained monotonic ramps, extreme outliers (>5 robust units), or irregular spike timing.
